name: Wilted Heart
description: A wilted flower with a broken heart is a romance that has dried out. People use it for a breakup, a love that faded, or a gesture that arrived too late.
meaning: The drooping flower is what remains and the broken heart is the injury. Together they mean an ending that is sad, used up, or past the point of a fresh bouquet.
examples: the flowers from March are a metaphor now 🥀💔
I kept the stem and I should not have 🥀💔
this is the quiet kind of over 🥀💔
seoDescription: What does 🥀💔 mean? A romance that faded or ended: sad, dried out, and past the fresh-bouquet stage.

longForm.overview:
A wilted rose and a broken heart describe an ending that did not happen in one dramatic slam. 🥀💔 is the faded version. People send it when a relationship dried up, when an apology showed up after the feeling was gone, or when they are looking at literal dead flowers and letting them stand for the month they just had. The broken heart is the pain. The wilt is the time. Something was fresh once, and the sender is telling you that window closed.

It is quieter than ice cream and a broken heart. That pair is a person actively comforting themselves. This pair is a person stating a condition. Friends read 🥀💔 as "do not try to revive this tonight." Exes sometimes send it as a last word that asks for no reply. The flower being dead matters: a fresh bouquet would mean a gesture still in motion. A wilted one means the gesture, or the love, sat too long. Treat the message as past-tense even if the sender is still hurting in the present.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
People put 🥀💔 on a final text, on a story they will archive, or under a photo of a vase they are finally throwing out. It shows up in song-lyric posts and in very plain announcements.

Mutual friends use it carefully when explaining why they will not pass along another message. The wilt means they consider the chapter shut.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not send 🥀💔 about a fight that both of you still expect to resolve this weekend. The dead flower tells the other person you have left the repair window.

Skip it for a plant that literally needs water, unless you are making the joke obvious. Most readers will see a breakup first.
longForm.howToReply:
If you are a friend, acknowledge the ending and ask what they need this week. Do not offer to text the ex.

If you are the ex, silence may be the request. A long defense will read as ignoring the wilt. One respectful line is the most the pair invites.

faqs.question: What does 🥀💔 mean?
faqs.answer: 🥀💔 means a love or a gesture has withered. The relationship is ending, or it already ended, and the sadness is quiet.

faqs.question: Is 🥀💔 worse than 💔?
faqs.answer: It is more specific. A broken heart can be fresh. The wilted flower adds time: this sat too long to save easily.

faqs.question: Can 🥀💔 mean a dead plant?
faqs.answer: Only with words that say so. Without them, people assume a romance faded.

faqs.question: Should I reply to an ex who sent 🥀💔?
faqs.answer: Usually with very little, or with nothing. The pair often means the conversation itself has dried up.

conversationExamples.message: I am not angry. I am 🥀💔. please stop sending plans
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are closing the relationship and the calendar. Stop proposing dates. A brief acknowledgment respects the line they drew.

conversationExamples.message: threw the vase out. 🥀💔 and a long walk
conversationExamples.interpretation: Your friend is marking an ending with a small physical act. Offer the walk or offer quiet. Do not suggest they text the other person.

conversationExamples.message: some songs are just 🥀💔 and that is the review
conversationExamples.interpretation: They may be talking about music, using the pair as a mood. You can name a song. Do not assume their own relationship ended unless they say it did.

conversationExamples.message: your sister is home. it is 🥀💔 and she does not want questions tonight
conversationExamples.interpretation: You are being asked to protect someone's privacy. Keep the household gentle and do not interview her.
